A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same brain-tuning research. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and the original methods and analyses can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original brain-alignment, downstream-task, and semantic-phonetic preference experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and reports additional acoustic prediction, baseline comparison, and model/data-size results in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains average pooling, a linear fMRI prediction head, L2 reconstruction loss, a frozen feature extractor, and transformer fine-tuning. The added baselines, model-size experiments, and clarification of voxel composition do not establish changes to the proposed brain-tuning procedure.

E1.justification: The fMRI dataset, original downstream datasets and tasks, and semantic-phonetic word set are retained. Appendix D.1 adds MFCC and FBANK prediction on TIMIT, a limited extension into acoustic reconstruction tasks without adding a new corpus or population.

E2.justification: v3 adds stimulus-tuned, GPT2-Medium-tuned, and Llama2-7B-tuned Wav2vec2.0 comparisons (Figure 10). Pretrained HuBERT Large, previously compared for brain alignment, also enters downstream comparisons (Figure 11). Random-fMRI and BigSLM controls are retained under revised names.

E3.justification: New protocols include acoustic regression probes evaluated with R2, HuBERT sizes of 90M, 317M, and 1B parameters, and Wav2vec2.0 training with 20%, 50%, 70%, and 100% of brain-tuning data. New stimulus/text-model controls use 200 epochs. The original story split and principal evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of acoustic-capability retention (Figure 9), whether extra stimulus training explains improvements and which tasks benefit from text-model supervision (Figure 10), and sensitivity to model/data size (Figure 12). Expanded participant-specific brain maps further examine consistency of the retained alignment findings.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors across participants and use Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with p < 0.05 for alignment and low-level-impact comparisons. No new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals, or statistical testing methods are documented.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 retain their plotted results. Added findings include largely preserved acoustic prediction, stimulus-tuning near pretrained performance, Llama2-tuning slightly exceeding brain-tuning on two Wav2vec2.0 tasks, and declining gains with less data or larger models at fixed data. Section 4.3 also changes its description of BigSLM from generally equal/worse to equal/better without changing Figure 4 values.

T1.justification: The normalized-alignment definition, low-level-impact equation, and semantic-phonetic distance-difference definition remain unchanged. v3 introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the downstream claim from five tasks thought to require semantic understanding to tasks helped by semantic understanding. The central semantic-improvement claim, three-family validation, and claimed first demonstration of downstream benefits from brain alignment remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds text-model controls to support its interpretation of task semantics and interprets acoustic probes as evidence against catastrophic forgetting. Section 5 proposes a mechanism involving both auditory and late-language voxels, explicitly leaving region-only tuning effects as hypotheses. Appendix E.2 adds qualifications concerning data availability and diminishing gains with larger models.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly documents spectral bands, diphone encodings, articulatory features, and annotation sources. Appendix D.2 specifies baseline matching, stimulus-tuning losses and learning-rate schedule, 200-epoch budgets, and text-model layer selection. These substantially expand reproducibility information; code release remains promised rather than documented as available.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Gong et al. (2023), GPT2 by Radford et al. (2019), and Llama2 by Touvron et al. (2023). It also explicitly positions stimulus tuning relative to Merlin and Toneva (2022). The main related-work discussion and relationship to Schwartz et al. (2019) remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect noise-ceiling explanations, downstream results, and discussion. v3 introduces a comparison-model subsection, standardizes baseline names, expands appendix organization, and adds acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9–13 for acoustic probes, additional comparisons, scaling, and voxel selection. Original appendix brain maps move to Figures 14–15 and expand from one to five participants each. Existing figures also receive revised legends, sizing, and brain-region annotations.

improvement.justification: Appendix D addresses important gaps in v1 by directly testing whether extra audio explains the gains and whether improved semantics sacrifices acoustic capabilities. Text-model controls, scaling analyses, and fuller implementation details substantially strengthen validation of the central claim. The voxel mechanism remains untested, and declining gains with larger models qualify the discussion's scaling optimism, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
